text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement (I): On nitration of m-xylene with $\mathrm{HNO}_{3},\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ followed by oxidation, 4-nitrobenzene-1,3-dicarboxylic acid is obtained as the major product.

Statement (II) : $-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$ group is o/p-directing while $-\mathrm{NO}_{2}$ group is m-directing group.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I : Correct


[IMG]


Nitration of m-xylene follows electrophilic aromatic substitution mechanism. First step is the generation of electrophile NO${}_{2}^{+}$ (nitronium ion) and then the electrophile attacks the benzene ring. Methyl groups are ortho-para directing groups. The NO${}_{2}^{+}$ in ortho position is not possible in this case due to the two neighbouring methyl groups. The nitro group is bonded to the para-position.

On oxidation, the methyl groups get converted to carboxylic acid groups. ($-$CH${}_{3}$ to $-$COOH conversion). So, the statement is correct.

Statement II : Correct

$-$CH${}_{3}$ group (methyl group) is ortho-para directing and $-$NO${}_{2}$ group (nitro group) is meta directing.

$-$CH${}_{3}$ group $⟶$ electron donating group

$-$NO${}_{2}$ group $⟶$ electron withdrawing group.

Electron donating groups push electrons towards the ring and increase electron density. Electron donating groups give ortho-para directing products. Electron withdrawing groups pull electrons away from the ring and decrease electron density. Electron withdrawing groups give meta-directing products. So, the statement is correct.

So, both statement I and statement II are true.

solution.body:

Histidine

Isoleucine

Leucine

Lysine

Methionine

Phenylalanine

Threonine

Valine

From the provided list:

Valine (A) is essential.

Proline (B) is non-essential.

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement (I): NaCl is added to the ice at 0°C, present in the ice cream box to prevent the melting of ice cream.

Statement (II): On addition of NaCl to ice at 0°C, there is a depression in freezing point.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
NaCl dissolves in the film of water on the ice and forms brine, whose freezing point lies below $0^{\circ }\text{C}$ (depression in freezing point, a colligative property). So Statement II is true.

At $0^{\circ }\text{C}$ the ice is above the freezing point of the brine, so it melts. The latent heat of fusion it absorbs is drawn from the mixture itself, and the ice–salt mixture cools well below $0^{\circ }\text{C}$ (a freezing mixture, down to about $-21^{\circ }\text{C}$).

Ice cream is itself a solution and freezes below $0^{\circ }\text{C}$, so plain ice at $0^{\circ }\text{C}$ cannot keep it hard; the colder ice–salt mixture keeps drawing heat from it and keeps it frozen. The salt melts the ice but prevents the melting of the ice cream, so Statement I is true.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement (I): In partition chromatography, stationary phase is thin film of liquid present in the inert support.

Statement (II): In paper chromatography, the material of paper acts as a stationary phase.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement (I) is true.

In partition chromatography, the separation is based on the partition of substances between two liquid phases. One liquid phase is held as a thin film on an inert solid support. This liquid film acts as the stationary phase.

Statement (II) is false.

Paper chromatography is a type of partition chromatography. In it, the paper mainly acts as an inert support. The actual stationary phase is the water trapped in the fibres of the chromatography paper, not the material of the paper itself.

So, the correct answer is:

Option A: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
0.1 M solution of KI reacts with excess of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ and $\mathrm{KIO}_{3}$ solutions. According to equation

$5\mathrm{I}^{-}+\mathrm{IO}_{3}^{-}+6\mathrm{H}^{+}\to 3\mathrm{I}_{2}+3\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

Identify the correct statements :

(A) 200 mL of KI solution reacts with 0.004 mol of $\mathrm{KIO}_{3}$

(B) 200 mL of KI solution reacts with 0.006 mol of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$

(C) 0.5 L of KI solution produced 0.005 mol of $\mathrm{I}_{2}$

(D) Equivalent weight of $\mathrm{KIO}_{3}$ is equal to ( $\frac{\text{Molecular weight}}{5}$ )

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Molarity of KI = 0.1 M

$5I^{-}+IO_{3}^{-}+6H^{+}\to 3I_{2}+3H_{2}O$ (balanced chemical equation)

$5KI+KIO_{3}+3H_{2}SO_{4}\to 3I_{2}+3K_{2}SO_{4}+3H_{2}O$

(A) Volume given (KI) = 200 mL = 0.2 L

Molarity (KI) = 0.1 M or mol L${}^{-1}$

The molarity formula is used here to calculate the number of moles of K.I.

Molarity, $M=\frac{numberofmoles}{volumeinL}$

So, number of moles = Molarity $\times$ Volume in L

For the given volume of KI,

number of moles = 0.1 mol L${}^{-1}$ $\times$ 0.2 L

= 0.02 mol

The stoichiometric ratio between KI and KIO${}_{3}$ is

$KI:KIO_{3}$

$I^{-}:IO_{3}^{-}$

$5:1$

$1:\frac{1}{5}$

For one mol $I^{-},\frac{1}{5}$ mol  $IO_{3}^{-}$ is used.

So, for 0.02 mol I${}^{-}$,

Moles of $IO_{3}^{-}=0.02\times \frac{1}{5}=0.004$ mol

The statement (A) is correct.

(B) Volume given (KI) = 200 mL = 0.2 L

Molarity (KI) = 0.1 M

number of moles of KI (I${}^{-}$) = Molarity $\times$ Volume (L)

$=0.1molL^{-1}\times 0.2L=0.02mol$

The stoichiometric ratio between KI and $H_{2}SO_{4}$ is

$KI:H_{2}SO_{4}$

$5:3$

$1:\frac{3}{5}$ {3 moles $H_{2}SO_{4}$ can give 6H${}^{+}$}

$I^{-},\frac{3}{5}$

For one mol $I^{-},\frac{3}{5}$ mol $H_{2}SO_{4}$ is used.

So, for 0.02 mol I${}^{-}$,

moles of $H_{2}SO_{4}=0.02\times \frac{3}{5}=0.012$ mol

This statement is not correct.

(C) Volume given (KI) = 0.5 L

Molarity (KI) = 0.1 M

Number of moles of KI = Molarity $\times$ Volume

$=0.1molL^{-1}\times 0.5L=0.05mol$

The stoichiometric ratio between I${}^{-}$ and I${}_{2}$ is

$KI:I_{2}$

$I^{-}:I_{2}$

$5:3$

$1:\frac{3}{5}$

For 1 mol $I^{-},\frac{3}{5}$ mol I${}_{2}$ is produced.

So, for 0.05 mol, moles of $I_{2}=0.05\times \frac{3}{5}=0.03$ mol

This statement is not correct.

(D) Equivalent weight of $KIO_{3}=\frac{Molecularweight}{5}$

This statement is correct.

Equivalent weight $=\frac{Molecularweight}{Valencyfactor\to numberofelectrons}$

Here, valency factor = 5

Each KIO${}_{3}$ molecule gains 5 electrons in this reaction.

KIO${}_{3}$ acts as the oxidising agent, gains electrons from the iodide ion in KI.

When KIO${}_{3}$ is reduced to I${}_{2}$ each molecule gains 5 electrons. So, the valency factor is 5 and equivalent weight is lower than molecular weight.

This statement is correct.

Correct statements are A and D.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: The type of oxide formed by the element among Li, Na, Be, Mg, B and Al that has the least atomic radius is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Atomic radius decreases across a period and increases down a group. The atomic radii are Li 152, Be 111, B 88 pm (period 2) and Na 186, Mg 160, Al 143 pm (period 3).

Boron, the period-2 element farthest to the right in the set, therefore has the least atomic radius.

Boron ($1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{1}$) has three valence electrons and shows the +3 oxidation state, so its oxide is $\mathrm{B}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}$, of the type $\mathrm{A}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$ (the types $\mathrm{AO}$, $\mathrm{AO}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{A}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ correspond to +2, +4 and +1).

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: Which one of the following reaction sequences will give an azo dye?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An azo dye forms when an aryl diazonium ion couples with a strongly activated arene (a phenol or an aromatic amine), giving $\mathrm{Ar}-\mathrm{N}=\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{Ar}{}^{'}$.

(A) $\mathrm{SOCl}{}_{2}$ converts benzenesulphonic acid into benzenesulphonyl chloride, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{SO}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}$; $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ gives benzenesulphonamide, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{SO}{}_{2}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$, which benzyl chloride alkylates to $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{SO}{}_{2}\mathrm{NHCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}$. No $-\mathrm{N}=\mathrm{N}-$ bond forms.

(B) 70% $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ hydrolyses benzonitrile to benzoic acid, $\mathrm{PCl}{}_{5}$ converts it into benzoyl chloride and aniline then gives benzanilide, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CONHC}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}$. No azo bond forms.

(C) $\mathrm{Sn}/\mathrm{HCl}$ reduces nitrobenzene to aniline; $\mathrm{NaNO}{}_{2}/\mathrm{HCl}$ at 0–5 °C diazotises it to benzenediazonium chloride, which couples with β-naphthol in $\mathrm{NaOH}$ at C-1 to give 1-phenylazo-2-naphthol, an orange azo dye.


[IMG]

(D) The benzenediazonium ion is a weak electrophile and does not couple with toluene, whose methyl group activates the ring far too weakly; no azo dye forms.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
Identify the homoleptic complexes with odd number of $d$ electrons in the central metal :

(A) $[\mathrm{FeO}_{4}]^{2-}$

(B) $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-}$

(C) $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{5}\mathrm{NO}]^{2-}$

(D) $[\mathrm{CoCl}_{4}]^{2-}$

(E) $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{3}\mathrm{F}_{3}]$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Homoleptic complexes are complexes with identical ligands attached to the central metal atom.

(A) $[FeO_{4}]^{2-}$ - Homoleptic

Central metal : Fe

In this complex, Fe is in +6 oxidation state.

{oxidation state : $x+4(-2)=-2$

$x-8=-2$

$x=-2+6=+6$

Configuration of $Fe-d^{6}s^{2}$

Configuration of $Fe(+6)-d^{2}$

Iron has even number of d electrons. So, it is not correct.

(B) $[Fe(CN)_{6}]^{3-}$ -  Homoleptic

Central metal : Fe

In this complex, the oxidation state of Fe is +3

Oxidation state :

$x+6(-1)=-3$

$x-6=-3$

$x=-3+6=+3$

Configuration of $Fe-d^{6}s^{2}$

Configuration of $Fe(+3)-d^{5}$

Iron has odd number of d electrons.

So, it is correct.

(C) $[Fe(CN)_{5}NO]^{2-}$ - Not homoleptic

This complex has different type of ligands.

(D) $[CoCl_{4}]^{2-}$ - Homoleptic

Central metal - Co

In this complex, the oxidation state of Co is +2

Oxidation state:

$x+4(-1)=-2$

$x-4=-2$

$x=-2+4=+2$

Configuration of $Co-d^{7}s^{2}$

Configuration of $Co(+2)-d^{7}$

Cobalt has odd number of d electrons.

So, it is correct.

(E) $[Co(H_{2}O)_{3}F_{3}]$ - Not homoleptic,

It has different type of ligands.

Complexes B and D are homoleptic complexes with odd number of d electrons in the central metal. So, correct answer is

(B) and (D) only.

text:
Match List - I with List - II :

  
    List - I (Applications)
    List - II (Batteries/Cell)
  
  
    (A) Transistors
    (I) Anode - Zn/Hg; Cathode - HgO + C
  
  
    (B) Hearing aids
    (II) Hydrogen fuel cell
  
  
    (C) Inverters
    (III) Anode - Zn; Cathode - Carbon
  
  
    (D) Apollo space ship
    (IV) Anode - Pb; Cathode - Pb | PbO$_{2}$
  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For each application listed in List-I, match it with the appropriate battery or cell type from List-II based on their characteristics:

(A) Transistors: Generally use a dry cell or Leclanché cell, where the anode is zinc (Zn) and the cathode is a carbon rod surrounded by manganese dioxide (MnO₂).  

Therefore, (A) Transistors match with (III) Anode - Zn; Cathode - Carbon.

(B) Hearing aids: Operate using a mercury cell. The anode in this cell is a zinc-mercury amalgam, and the cathode is composed of mercury oxide (HgO) with carbon.  

Thus, (B) Hearing aids match with (I) Anode - Zn/Hg; Cathode - HgO + C.

(C) Inverters: Use a lead-acid storage cell. In this type of cell, the anode consists of lead (Pb), and the cathode is a lead dioxide (PbO₂) grid.  

As a result, (C) Inverters match with (IV) Anode - Pb; Cathode - Pb | PbO₂.

(D) Apollo space ship: Utilizes a hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell. The hydrogen is oxidized at the anode, while oxygen is reduced at the cathode.  

Therefore, (D) Apollo space ship matches with (II) Hydrogen fuel cell.

Summary of matches:

A - III

B - I

C - IV

D - II

This corresponds with Answer Option A.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: Which one of the following, with HBr will give a phenol?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A phenol forms only if the oxygen left after cleavage is attached directly to the benzene ring.

(A) Anisole: the protonated ether is attacked by $\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$ at the methyl carbon ($S_{N}2$), while the aryl $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}$ bond, with partial double-bond character, is not broken:

$\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}+\mathrm{HBr}\longrightarrow \mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{OH}+\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{Br}$

(B) $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$ is an acetal; HBr breaks only its alkyl $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}$ bonds, and no oxygen is attached to the ring.

(C) $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}$ cleaves at the tert-butyl group ($S_{N}1$) to $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{CBr}$ and benzyl alcohol, not phenol.

(D) $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ cleaves at the benzylic carbon to $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Br}$ and $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{OH}$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: The calculated spin-only magnetic moments of $K_{3}[Fe(OH)_{6}]$ and $K_{4}[Fe(OH)_{6}]$ respectively are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$K_{3}[Fe(OH)_{6}]$

$K_{4}[Fe(OH)_{6}]$

Spin-only magnetic moment formula is $\sqrt{n(n+2)}$, where n is the number of unpaired electrons in the central metal $K_{3}[Fe(OH)_{6}]$

Also written as $[Fe(OH)_{6}]^{3-}$

Oxidation state of $Fe\to +3$

Configuration of $Fe\to d^{6}s^{2}$

Configuration of $Fe^{3+}\to d^{5}$

Since OH${}^{-}$ is a weak ligand, no pairing of electrons occurs.


[IMG]


Unpaired electrons, $n=5$

So, spin-only magnetic moment

$=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$

$=\sqrt{5(5+2)}$

$=\sqrt{5\times 7}$

$=\sqrt{35}$

$=5.92$ BM

$3(+1)+x+6(-1)=0$

$3+x-6=0$

$x-3=0$

$x=+3$

$K_{4}[Fe(OH)_{6}]$

$4(+1)+x+6(-1)=0$

$4+x-6=0$

$x=6-4=+2$

Also written as $[Fe(OH)_{6}]^{4-}$

Oxidation state of $Fe\to +2$

Configuration of $Fe\to d^{6}s^{2}$

Configuration of $Fe^{+2}\to d^{6}$

Since OH${}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, no pairing of electrons occurs.


[IMG]


Unpaired electrons = 4

Spin-only magnetic moment

$=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$

$=\sqrt{4(4+2)}$

$=\sqrt{4\times 6}$

$=\sqrt{24}$

$=4.90$ BM

Spin-only magnetic moments of $K_{3}[Fe(OH)_{6}]$ and $K_{4}[Fe(OH)_{6}]$ respectively are 5.92 and 4.90 B.M.

Correct answer is option (3) 5.92 and 4.90 B.M.

text:
Consider the equilibrium

$\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g})+3\mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{g})⇌\mathrm{CH}_{4}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})$

If the pressure applied over the system increases by two fold at constant temperature then

(A) Concentration of reactants and products increases.

(B) Equilibrium will shift in forward direction.

(C) Equilibrium constant increases since concentration of products increases.

(D) Equilibrium constant remains unchanged as concentration of reactants and products remain same.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given equilibrium

$\mathrm{C}\mathrm{O}_{(\mathrm{g})}+3\mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{g})_{(\mathrm{n}=4)}⇌\mathrm{C}\mathrm{H}_{4}_{(\mathrm{g})}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})_{(\mathrm{n}=2)}$

Temperature $\to$ Constant

Pressure $\to$ Increases by two fold.

It is based on Le Chatelier's principle. The principle states that if a change of condition is applied to a system in equilibrium, the system will shift in a direction that relieves the stress.

When pressure increases in a chemical equilibrium, the equilibrium shifts towards the side of the reaction with fewer moles of gas molecules. According to the principle, the reaction will favor the side that provides fewer gas molecules to counteract the increased pressure.

In this equilibrium, fewer gas molecules are on the product side and on increase in pressure, equilibrium shifts towards products - forward reaction occurs. As a result, concentration of the products increases.

A) Concentration of reactants and products increases.

$-$ Correct

With increase in pressure, at constant temperature, the concentration of both reactants and products will increase because the same amount of gas is now in a smaller volume.

(B) Equilibrium will shift in forward direction

Correct

Increase in pressure causes product formation as the equilibrium shift is in the forward direction.

(C) Equilibrium constant increases since concentration of products increases.

Not correct.

The expression for equilibrium constant (K${}_{c}$) for the given equilibrium can be written as

$K_{c}=\frac{[CH_{4}][H_{2}O]}{[CO][H_{2}]^{3}}$

Equilibrium constant is not changed with increase in pressure and increase in concentration of reactants or products.

So, the equilibrium constant value is not affected by change in concentration. If the change increase in concentration of product takes place, the equilibrium position will be shifted to counteract the change. So, equilibrium const value does not increase. Statement is incorrect.

(D) Equilibrium constant remains unchanged as concentration of reactants and products remain same.

Statement is incorrect.

In the reaction, increase in pressure causes changes in the concentration of reactants and products but the equilibrium constant will not change.

Statements (A) and (B) are correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: First ionisation enthalpy values of first four group 15 elements are given below as the options. Choose the correct value for the element that is a main component of apatite family :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Apatite family - A group of phosphate minerals that includes fluorapatite, chlorapatite, and hydroxyapatite. Chemical formula $Ca_{10}(PO_{4})_{6}(OH,F,Cl)_{2}$

$\left. \begin{array}{l} Fluorapatite\to Ca_{10}(PO_{4})_{6}F_{2} \\ Chlorapatite\to Ca_{10}(PO_{4})_{6}Cl_{2} \\ Hydroxyapatite\to Ca_{10}(PO_{4})_{6}(OH)_{2} \end{array}\right \{\begin{array}{l} Maincomponents: \\ Calciumandphosphate \end{array}$

So, the element considered is phosphorus.

The first four group 15 elements are Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), Arsenic (As) and Antimony (Sb). The outer configuration of phosphorus is half filled and hence stable $(s^{2}p^{3})$.

For a stable configuration, ionization enthalpy is high. Ionization enthalpy - Energy required to remove an electron from the gaseous atom.

Nitrogen has the highest first ionization enthalpy in group 15.

Down the group, ionization enthalpy decreases.

Down the group, atomic size increases, valence electrons are less attracted to the nucleus. And here, electron removal will become easier. So, ionization enthalpy also decreases.

The highest value of ionization enthalpy 1402 KJ mol${}^{-1}$ corresponds to nitrogen element.

So, the first ionization enthalpy of the element that is a main component of apatite family is option D) 1012 kJ mol${}^{-1}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
For hydrogen like species, which of the following graphs provides the most appropriate representation of E vs Z plot for a constant n?

[E : Energy of the stationary state, Z : atomic number, n = principal quantum number]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$EvsZplot(cons\tan tn)\left \{\begin{array}{l} E-Energyofthestationarystate \\ Z-atomicnumber \\ n-\mathrm{Pr}incipalquantumnumber \end{array} \right.$

The formula of energy of hydrogen like species is

$E=-13.6\frac{z^{2}}{n^{2}}eV$

$E\propto -\frac{z^{2}}{n^{2}}$

For constant n, $E\propto -Z^{2}$

Here, E and Z has a quadratic relationship. Since the equation (proportionality) includes a negative sign, the graph of E vs Z will be a downward - opening parabola.


[IMG]


The graph is like an upside down U. In the given options, graph 4 is like half upside down parabola.


[IMG]

text:
If C (diamond) $\to$ C (graphite) $+X\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

C (diamond) $+\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\to \mathrm{CO}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{Y}\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}{}^{-1}$

C (graphite) $+\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\to \mathrm{CO}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{Z}\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

at constant temperature. Then
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A heat term written on the product side is heat evolved, so the enthalpy changes are:

$\text{C(diamond)}\to \text{C(graphite)}$; $\Delta H_{1}=-X$

$\text{C(diamond)}+\mathrm{O}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\longrightarrow \mathrm{CO}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$; $\Delta H_{2}=-Y$

$\text{C(graphite)}+\mathrm{O}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\longrightarrow \mathrm{CO}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$; $\Delta H_{3}=-Z$

Subtracting the third equation from the second gives the first, so by Hess's law $\Delta H_{1}=\Delta H_{2}-\Delta H_{3}$:

$-X=-Y+Z\Rightarrow X=Y-Z$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement (I): It is impossible to specify simultaneously with arbitrary precision, both the linear momentum and the position of a particle.

Statement (II) : If the uncertainty in the measurement of position and uncertainty in measurement of momentum are equal for an electron, then the uncertainty in the measurement of velocity is $⩾\sqrt{\frac{h}{π}}\times \frac{1}{2m}$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I is Heisenberg's uncertainty principle: the position and the momentum of a particle cannot both be determined simultaneously with arbitrary precision, because $\Delta x\cdot \Delta p\geq \dfrac{h}{4π}$. Statement I is true.

For Statement II, $\Delta x=\Delta p$, so

$(\Delta p)^{2}\geq \dfrac{h}{4π}\Rightarrow \Delta p\geq \sqrt{\dfrac{h}{4π}}=\dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{h}{π}}$

With $\Delta p=m\Delta v$,

$\Delta v\geq \dfrac{1}{2m}\sqrt{\dfrac{h}{π}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{h}{π}}\times \dfrac{1}{2m}$

so Statement II is true.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
Drug $X$ becomes ineffective after $50%$ decomposition. The original concentration of drug in a bottle was $16\mathrm{mg}/\mathrm{mL}$ which becomes $4\mathrm{mg}/\mathrm{mL}$ in 12 months. The expiry time of the drug in months is $_________$.

Assume that the decomposition of the drug follows first order kinetics.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Original concentration, $a=16$ mg/mL

Concentration at time

t = 12 months, $a-x=4$ mg/mL

For first order kinetics, the equation for rate constant

$k=\frac{2.303}{t}\log \frac{a}{a-x}$

a $\to$ Initial concentration

$a-x\to$ Concentration at time, t

$=\frac{2.303}{12months}\log \frac{16mg/mL}{4mg/mL}$

$=\frac{2.303}{12}\log 4$

$=0.1155months^{-1}$

Drug is ineffective after 50% decomposition. So, the expiry time is after 50% decomposition. The time at which 50% decomposition occurs in a reaction is known as half life $(t_{1/2})$. So, $t_{1/2}$ is the expiry time of the drug.

$t_{1/2}$ formula is

$t_{1/2}=\frac{0.693}{k}$

Substitute k = 0.1155 months${}^{-1}$,

$t_{1/2}=\frac{0.693}{0.1155}$ months

= 6 months

Expiry time can also be calculated as,

$t=\frac{2.303}{k}\log \frac{a}{a-x}$

Initial is taken as 100%

The percent at expiry time is 50%

$=\frac{2.303}{0.1155months^{-1}}\times \log \frac{100%}{50%}$

$=\frac{2.303}{0.1155}\times \log \frac{100}{50}$

$=\frac{2.303}{0.1155}\times 0.301$

$=6.002$

= 6 months

Correct answer is option (3) 6
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
$\mathrm{O}_{2}$ gas will be evolved as a product of electrolysis of :

(A) an aqueous solution of $\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$ using silver electrodes.

(B) an aqueous solution of $\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$ using platinum electrodes.

(C) a dilute solution of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ using platinum electrodes.

(D) a high concentration solution of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ using platinum electrodes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) With silver electrodes, the silver anode itself is oxidised, $\mathrm{Ag}\longrightarrow \mathrm{Ag}{}^{+}+\mathrm{e}{}^{-}$, and $\mathrm{Ag}{}^{+}+\mathrm{e}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{Ag}$ occurs at the cathode, so no $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ is formed.

(B) With platinum electrodes, $\mathrm{Ag}{}^{+}+\mathrm{e}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{Ag}$ occurs at the cathode; $\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}{}^{-}$ is not oxidised, so water is oxidised at the anode, $2~\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\longrightarrow \mathrm{O}{}_{2}+4\mathrm{H}{}^{+}+4\mathrm{e}{}^{-}$, and $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ is evolved.

(C) Dilute $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ with platinum electrodes gives $2~\mathrm{H}{}^{+}\qquad +2\mathrm{e}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{H}{}_{2}$ at the cathode and $2~\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\longrightarrow \mathrm{O}{}_{2}+4\mathrm{H}{}^{+}+4\mathrm{e}{}^{-}$ ($E^{\circ }=1.23\text{V}$) at the anode, so $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ is evolved.

(D) In concentrated $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$, sulfate ions are oxidised at the platinum anode in preference to water, $2~\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{S}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{8}{}^{2-}+2\mathrm{e}{}^{-}$ ($E^{\circ }=1.96\text{V}$), giving peroxodisulfate instead of $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$.

Thus $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ is evolved in (B) and (C) only.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: Total number of non-bonded electrons present in $NO_{2}^{-}$ ion based on Lewis theory is $______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
NO${}_{2}^{-}$ ion


[IMG]


Structure (Lewis Structure)

Nitrogen (N) has 2 non-bonding electrons. The total valence electrons of N is 5. Out of 5, 3 electrons are bonding electrons and 2 electrons are non-bonding electrons.

Double bonded oxygen has 4 non-bonding electrons. Oxygen valence electrons : 6

Out of 6, 2 are bonding electrons are 4 are non-bonding electrons.

Negatively charged oxygen has 6 non-bonding electrons. The negative charge is due to the extra electron present. So, the total number of non-bonded electrons present in NO${}_{2}^{-}$ ion based on Lewis theory is

$2(of\qquad N)+4(ofO)+6(ofO^{-})$

$=2+4+6=12$

text:
Consider the following low-spin complexes

$\mathrm{K}_{3}[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NO}_{2})_{6}],\mathrm{K}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}],\mathrm{K}_{3}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}],\mathrm{Cu}_{2}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]\text{and}\mathrm{Zn}_{2}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]$

The sum of the spin-only magnetic moment values of complexes having yellow colour is $________ B.M. ($answer in nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Of the given complexes, $\mathrm{K}{}_{3}[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}){}_{6}]$ is yellow and $\mathrm{K}{}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]$ is yellow (yellow prussiate of potash), while $\mathrm{K}{}_{3}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]$ is red, $\mathrm{Cu}{}_{2}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]$ is chocolate brown and $\mathrm{Zn}{}_{2}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]$ is bluish white.

In $\mathrm{K}{}_{3}[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}){}_{6}]$, cobalt is $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ ($3d^{6}$); the low-spin configuration $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$ has $n=0$ unpaired electrons.

In $\mathrm{K}{}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]$, iron is $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$ ($3d^{6}$); the low-spin configuration $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$ again has $n=0$.

With $μ=\sqrt{n(n+2)}\text{BM}$, both yellow complexes have $μ=0$, so the sum is $0+0=0\text{BM}$.

Hence, the answer is 0.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
In the sulphur estimation, 0.20 g of a pure organic compound gave 0.40 g of barium sulphate. The percentage of sulphur in the compound is $__________$ $\times 10^{-1}%$.

(Molar mass : $\mathrm{O}=16,\mathrm{S}=32,\mathrm{Ba}=137$ in $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mass of pure organic compound = 0.20 g

Mass of barium sulphate obtained = 0.40 g

% of sulphur in the compound = ?

Molar mass of $BaSO_{4}=137gmol^{-1}+32gmol^{-1}+(16\times 4)gmol^{-1}=233gmol^{-1}$

Moles of $BaSO_{4}:$

Moles $=\frac{mass}{molarmass}$

$=\frac{0.40g}{233gmol^{-1}}=0.001717mol$

Moles of sulphur:

From the formula $BaSO_{4}$, 1 mole of $BaSO_{4}$ contains 1 mole of sulphur (s). Therefore, the moles of sulphur in the sample is equal to the moles of $BaSO_{4}$.

Moles of S = 0.001717 mol

Mass of sulphur :

Mass = moles $\times$ molar mass

Moles of S = 0.001717 mol, substitute this value as

Mass of S = 0.001717 mol $\times$ 32 g mol${}^{-1}$.

= 0.054944 g

Percentage of sulphur in the organic compound:

The formula is

Percentage of $S=\frac{massofS}{massoforganiccompound}\times 100$

Substituting the values,

Percentage of $S=\frac{0.054944g}{0.20g}\times 100$

$=0.27472\times 100$

$=27.472%$

$=274.72\times 10^{-1}%$

$=275\times 10^{-1}%$

text: In the Claisen-Schmidt reaction to prepare dibenzalacetone from 5.3 g of benzaldehyde, a total of 3.51 g of product was obtained. The percentage yield in this reaction was $_______$ %.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mass of benzaldehyde = 5.3 g

Mass of product = 3.51 g

Claisen - Schmidt reaction :

Condensation of aromatic aldehydes / ketones (without alpha-hydrogen) with aliphatic aldehydes /ketones (with alpha-hydrogen) in the presence of weak base to form $α,β$-unsaturated aldehydes/ketones.

Given

benzaldehyde $\to$ dibenzalacetone


[IMG]


Formula of percent yield

Percent yield $=\frac{actualyield}{Theoreticalyield}\times 100$

Actual yield = 3.51 g

From the reaction, the stoichiometric ratio between benzaldehyde and dibenzal acetone is 2 : 1

benzaldehyde : dibenzalacetone

$2:1$

$1:\frac{1}{2}$

Moles of benzaldehyde:

$Moles=\frac{Mass}{Molarmass}$

$=\frac{5.3g}{106.12g/mol}$

= 0.04994 mol

Molarmass of benzaldehyde = 106.12 g/mol

For 1 mole of benzaldehyde, $\frac{1}{2}$ moles product (dibenzalacetone) is formed.

So, for 0.04994 mol benzaldehyde, $\frac{1}{2}\times 0.04994$ mol dibenzalacetone is formed.

So, moles of dibenzalacetone = 0.02497 mol

Mass of product dibenzalacetone (Theoretical yield)

Mass = moles $\times$ molarmass

$=0.02497$ mol $\times$ $234.29$ g/mol

= 5.850 g

Percent yield $=\frac{3.51g}{5.85g}\times 100$

$=0.6\times 100=60%$
